name: Jama Masjid
opening_hours: 7:00 AM - 12:00 PM, 1:30 PM - 6:30 PM daily (closed during namaz for non-Muslim visitors)
rules: Robes available at entrance if clothing is above knees or shoulders
Camera pass fee applicable for photography
visual_features: vast red sandstone courtyard with striped marble domes and two soaring minarets
description: The Masjid-i-Jehan-Numa, commonly known as the Jama Masjid, in Old Delhi area of Delhi, is one of the largest mosques in India. Its builder was the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, between 1644 and 1656, and it was inaugurated by its first Imam, Syed Abdul Ghafoor Shah Bukhari. Situated in the Mughal capital of Shahjahanabad, it served as the imperial mosque of the Mughal emperors until the demise of the empire in 1857. The Jama Masjid was regarded as a symbolic gesture of Mughal power across India. It was also a site of political significance during several key periods of British rule. It remains in active use, and is one of Delhi's most iconic sites, closely identified with the methods of Old Delhi. The mosque structure is a Monument of National Importance.
